video.title: Opus 5.5 vs GPT-6 is racing to the bottom..?
video.genre: AI explainer and opinion, partly screen-shared

protocol.note: Drafted from the transcript alone, without seeing any jevcut output or other labels.
protocol.times_from: Lemonfox transcript; seconds in the source, so labels survive re-transcription

clips.why: Hook: Opus 5.5 costs 40% of Fable 5.5 and GPT-6 Soul/Luna cost 50% less -- intelligence keeps getting cheaper. 'But is it really?' Opus dominates the cost Pareto frontier, but on the token-efficiency frontier GPT-6 does more with fewer tokens; payoff at 71.0: GPT-6 is more token efficient than Opus 5.5. 76.2 adds the label 'a tension between cost-efficient and token-efficient'. Several chart asides ('this dotted line here', 'as you can see') but the argument is spoken.

Hook as a question: from the consumer side, doesn't only cost matter, since Anthropic is cheaper per token -- 'right? Not quite.' API vs subscription split (OpenAI revenue mostly subscription, Anthropic mostly API); answer at 308.2: subscriptions are metered by tokens, API by cost. Two endings work: 333.5 spells out that user experience then depends on how token-hungry the model is (74s).

also_ok.why: Labs subsidize tokens at their discretion; the real tension is who pays for the inefficient tokens -- API users directly, subscribers are insulated; so token efficiency is a hedge against price competition. Works, but assumes the API-vs-subscription setup just before.

negatives.why: 3D plot of Opus 5.5 across cost/token/intelligence ('what you're seeing here', plateau at ~53): chart narration.
GPT-6 Soul/Luna/Astra trajectories on the same 3D plot, ending in a teaser question answered after the sponsor.
Other labs 'fighting in the cost axes, especially DeepSeek, as you can see': list of labs over a chart.
Closing thesis (falling cost doesn't mean more efficient underneath) delivered over quarter-by-quarter Pareto charts; the claim's support came minutes earlier.
